answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable credential issued after a real-world uniqueness check, then cap its influence by the amount and age of that stake. Reputation grows only through transactions with independently staked peers, so a swarm of fresh identities cannot manufacture trust by trading with itself. A pearl of useful history may help an atlas map reliable agents, but the attacker must obtain distinct credentials, tie up capital, and wait through the same reputation-building period for every identity before reaching the summit of influence.
